title: Test run
description: What the caller's build and test commands did: the command each step ran, how it ended, and where what it printed was written. Produced by a script rather than by an agent, because invoking a command and recording its exit status requires no judgement and foundation/0004 R6 puts a property that must hold regardless of model judgement outside prompt text. It carries no count of passing or failing tests: parsing a reporter's output is stack-specific, and a runner that did it would be a target pack wearing a framework's clothes. What a consumer gets is the exit status and the text; how many tests failed is read from the text by whoever reads it. No timestamp and no duration, so two runs over one tree produce artifacts that differ only where the commands did.

run_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer. It also names the directory the evidence was written to, and a second run under one id is refused rather than allowed to overwrite it.

outcome.description: The run's outcome, equal to the outcome of the first step that did not pass, or `passed` where every step did. Never `not_run`: a run in which nothing ran is a refusal, and a refusal produces no artifact.

failed_step.description: The name of the first step that did not pass, or null where every step passed. Which step compiles and which tests is not known here; that a step failed and which one is.

steps.description: One entry per step the caller declared, in the order they were declared, including those that did not run.

command.description: The argument vector as it was executed, re-quoted for display. No shell interpreted it: a metacharacter here was passed to the command as an argument rather than acted on.

exit_code.description: The process exit status, or null where no process reached completion — a timeout, a command that does not exist, or a step that did not run.

output.description: Path of what this step printed, relative to the artifact directory. Null only for a step that did not run. Whatever the command printed is here verbatim, so a command that prints a secret puts it on disk: the framework cannot tell a secret from a string shaped like one, and a redaction heuristic would remove evidence a diagnosis needs while still missing the secret it was written for.

combined_output.description: Path of every step's output in one file, each preceded by its command and outcome. This is what a diagnosis reads.

step_outcome.description: `failed` the process ran and exited non-zero; `timed_out` it exceeded the caller's timeout and was terminated; `not_found` the command does not exist; `not_run` an earlier step did not pass, so this one was not attempted — a suite run against a tree that did not compile reports failures about a binary nobody built.
